title: INT8 activation balance mapper and runtime fallback strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight activation 'balance map' and a runtime kernel fallback strategy to deploy activation-aware INT8 quantized variants with minimal accuracy regression and predictable latency. This ticket implements an end-to-end flow from offline calibration output (per-tensor/channel balance map) -> commitable quant profiles -> runtime routing + fused-op fallback kernels for operators that are poorly behaved under balanced quantization.
background: We observed models with KV-cache-heavy and layernorm-adjacent activations exhibiting larger accuracy variance under naive symmetric INT8 quantization. SmoothQuant-style activation redistribution reduces dynamic range mismatches, but production rollout requires: (1) reproducible calibration profiles per workload, (2) compact artifacts that fit our model catalog, and (3) runtime-safe fallbacks when optimized fused kernels introduce quality regressions for specific input shapes or sequence lengths.
proposed_solution: 1) Calibration harness emits a compact activation balance map (per-layer scale ratios + per-channel deltas) and a profile metadata file. 2) On model import, we generate two artifacts: a balanced-INT8 profile and a conservative fallback-INT8 profile (less aggressive balance). 3) Runtime can route requests by policy: prefer balanced profile for throughput-sensitive customers, automatically swap to fallback profile on quality regression detection, or route specific routes/keys to fallback. 4) Implement lightweight runtime kernel wrappers that detect shape/sequence patterns known to regress under balanced kernels and execute the conservative kernel path.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline produces a compact profile artifact (<= 128KB per model) and a human-readable summary
Average accuracy regression vs FP16 is <= 0.5% absolute on internal LM eval suite for 90% of evaluation prompts when using balanced profile
When fallback is triggered, accuracy returns to within 0.1% of FP16 baseline while P50 latency penalty <= 12% compared to balanced path
Runtime routing policy and canary rollout implemented in console (can target 1% traffic) with observability to flip back automatically
Unit + integration tests covering per-layer balance application, profile compatibility checks, and kernel fallback paths
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike complete - calibration harness prototype outputs per-layer scale ratios and per-channel variance heatmaps (not yet compacted). Linked spike notes in Confluence.

2025-02-20: Implemented profile serializer (JSON -> compressed binary). Initial binary is ~220KB for Llama-13B; need further compaction. Added compact encoding (delta-quantization) that reduces to ~110KB.

2025-02-26: PR opened for calibration harness and serializer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-pipeline/pull/312. CI passes for CPU unit tests, GPU integration tests still flaky on aarch64 runners.
2025-03-02: Runtime kernel wrapper prototype merged behind feature flag. Hooked routing policy into traffic router; created canary config in console (can target api-key/route).

2025-03-04: Internal eval across 12 workloads: balanced profile mean perplexity delta +0.4% (acceptable), fallback profile delta +0.08%. Observed P50 increase of 9% when fallback used; P95 unchanged in most cases. Details in evaluation spreadsheet.
test_plan: Offline: run calibration on representative dataset shards (chat, instruction, code) and record profile sizes and stability across seeds
Regression: run internal eval harness (lm-eval style) comparing FP16, balanced-INT8, fallback-INT8, and naive-INT8 across perplexity/ROUGE/EM where appropriate
Performance: microbenchmarks of kernel wrapper path vs fused balanced kernel for sequence lengths {64,128,512} and batch sizes {1,4,8}
Canary: deploy to 1% traffic for two customers (non-sensitive) and monitor accuracy regressions, token-level deltas, and latency SLO violations for 72 hours
Chaos: simulate node evictions and ensure routing to fallback does not increase error surface or lead to infinite routing loops
benchmarks: Llama-7B (seq=128, batch=1): balanced-INT8 P50=42ms, fallback-INT8 P50=46ms (9.5% increase), FP16 P50=48ms
Llama-13B (seq=256, batch=1): balanced-INT8 P50=68ms, fallback-INT8 P50=74ms (8.8% increase), FP16 P50=80ms
Accuracy (internal chat eval): FP16 perplexity=12.21, balanced-INT8=12.27 (+0.49%), fallback-INT8=12.22 (+0.08%)
Profile size: initial JSON=220KB -> compressed binary=110KB -> final delta-encoded=96KB
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Some fused kernels still produce silent degradations for edge sequence lengths. Mitigation: conservative fallback per-layer flag and runtime detection of shape signatures to force conservative kernels.

Risk: Profile explosion for multi-variant models (quantized, fp8, per-channel). Mitigation: canonicalization step to dedupe profiles and store deltas only for layers that differ from the model baseline.
Risk: Oscillation under automated routing (balanced -> fallback -> balanced). Mitigation: hysteresis policy (min time window + min requests) and metrics-driven cooldown.
Risk: Increased storage/transfer overhead for profiles. Mitigation: aggressive binary compression and CDN caching for hosted models.
next_steps: Finish compact encoding iteration (target <= 80KB) and add end-to-end protobuf schema for profile artifact
